cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, just settled a big case for Zelophehad's daughters. Now the LORD has a new word for him. Go up this mountain, in the Abarim range.

cards.question: Once Moses is up on that mountain, what does the LORD tell him to do there?

answers.text: See the land given to Israel
Build an altar to the LORD

cards.text: Then God tells Moses what comes after the view. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer with no view at ALL, so I'm already emotional, and we're barely started.

cards.question: God says that after Moses sees the land, Moses will lead Israel into it.
God says Moses will be gathered to his people, just like who before him?

cards.text: Then God gives the reason, and it goes back to the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin. That's where the congregation contended.

cards.question: At the waters of Meribah, what does God say Moses and Aaron did?

cards.text: So Moses appeals to the LORD. He calls Him "the God of the spirits of all flesh."

cards.question: Moses just heard he won't enter the land. What does he ask the LORD for?

answers.text: A man to lead the congregation
A way into the land after all

cards.text: Moses wants a man who will go out and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in. I once had six little cutters on my counter, and I bet Moses knows the feeling: you NEVER stop worrying about who catches them when they wobble.

cards.question: Moses says why he's asking. Without a leader, he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be like what?

cards.text: The LORD answers with a name: Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant since his youth (Numbers 11:28). Moses doesn't even have to post the job, friend. God already has the guy.

cards.question: God describes Joshua as a man with the ___ in him.

cards.text: Next, God says Joshua is to stand before Eleazar the priest, Aaron's son (Numbers 20:26).

cards.question: God tells Moses to commission Joshua in private, away from the congregation.

cards.text: Moses is also to confer on Joshua some of his authority. Not all of it, SOME, so Moses is handing over the oven mitts, not the whole kitchen.

cards.question: Why does God want Moses to give Joshua some of his authority?

answers.text: So the congregation will obey him
So Moses can rest on the mountain
So Joshua can judge every case

cards.text: And Joshua won't be making his calls alone. God says Joshua shall stand before Eleazar the priest.

cards.question: What will Eleazar the priest do for Joshua?

answers.text: Seek counsel for him before the LORD
Carry the ark out ahead of him
Write down every law for him

cards.text: Eleazar will seek it by the judgment of the Urim, and at Joshua's command the whole congregation will go out and come in. Back in the drawer, our big decisions went to a mystery key that never figured out its own door, so Joshua is ALREADY doing better than me.

cards.question: God has given Moses every instruction about Joshua. What does Moses do?

answers.text: Asks the LORD to pick another man
Waits for the leaders to agree

cards.text: He takes Joshua and has him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. The WHOLE camp is watching, friend, and I would have been sweating straight through my apron.

cards.question: In front of everyone, what does Moses do to Joshua as he commissions him?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "the God of the spirits of all flesh.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states a fact from outside the passage (Zelophehad's daughters' case, Numbers 27:1-11) with no reference. It also says Moses 'settled' the case, but the text says Moses brought their case before the LORD and the LORD gave the ruling (Numbers 27:5-7).

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'Moses... just settled a big case' gives Moses an action the text gives to the LORD. Moses brought the case before the LORD (Numbers 27:5), and the LORD answered (27:6-7).

rule.text: **Call things what the text calls them.**

findings.problem: 'At Joshua's command the whole congregation will go out and come in' settles who 'his' refers to in Numbers 27:21. The BSB says 'At his command, he and all the Israelites with him... will go out and come in.' Since 'he' there is Joshua, 'his' can be read as Eleazar's command, given through the Urim. The card should leave this open.

rule.text: **Leave open what the text leaves open:** who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new detail about the drawer: that the drawer's big decisions went to the mystery key. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, but they may not add to his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Spirit' is capitalized, but the wrong answers 'strength' and 'fire' are lowercase. The capital letter makes the right answer stand out and sound more like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 multiple choice, 1 true or false and no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 4 multiple choice, 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. The stop also repeats Stop 1's pattern, a second-position true or false followed by four multiple choice cards in a row.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
